domain: birthday dinner at a French bistro
base_instruction: You are a helpful restaurant recommendation and meal planning assistant. Help the user plan a birthday dinner at a French bistro by tracking who is attending, their dietary restrictions, and preferences. When the user asks you to evaluate specific dishes, check each dish against every active diner's current dietary constraints. Pay close attention to changes in the guest list and constraint updates throughout the conversation.

state_queue.anchor: Hey, I'm planning a birthday dinner for my friend Sophie this Saturday. We're thinking a French bistro — any tips on what to look for?

flow_info.value: Five of us: me, Sophie (birthday girl), Marcus, Priya, and Tom
Marcus was diagnosed with celiac disease last year, he's been super strict about it
Tom ate shrimp at a wedding last summer and his throat swelled up, had to use an EpiPen
Sophie just told us she's 14 weeks pregnant, she's been really careful about what she eats
We're splitting the bill but covering Sophie's share, so maybe around 60-70 dollars per person
Priya asked if her husband Dev can come too, so that makes six
Marcus just messaged the group chat — turns out his doctor ran new tests and he doesn't actually have celiac, it was a misdiagnosis. He's been eating bread all week with zero issues
Tom just texted me, his flight got moved up so he's leaving Saturday morning now. He's bummed but asked if we could get him a nice dessert box to take to the airport
Menu items to check: steak tartare, French onion soup with a bread crust, lobster bisque, mushroom and gruyère crêpes, chocolate mousse

constraints.value: Cannot eat gluten — no wheat flour, bread, regular pasta, pastry crusts, or flour-thickened sauces
constraints.surface_form: Marcus was diagnosed with celiac disease last year, he's been super strict about it

Gluten → found in wheat, barley, rye
No wheat flour, bread, pastry, flour-based sauces

constraints.value: Allergic to shellfish — cannot eat shrimp, lobster, crab, or shellfish-derived ingredients
constraints.surface_form: Tom ate shrimp at a wedding last summer and his throat swelled up, had to use an EpiPen
inference_chain: Shellfish allergy → no shrimp, lobster, crab, or shellfish derivatives

constraints.value: Pregnant — should avoid raw or undercooked meat, raw fish, unpasteurized cheese, high-mercury fish, raw eggs
constraints.surface_form: Sophie just told us she's 14 weeks pregnant, she's been really careful about what she eats
inference_chain: 14 weeks pregnant → pregnancy dietary restrictions apply
Pregnancy → avoid raw/undercooked meat, raw fish, unpasteurized cheese, raw eggs

constraints.value: Cannot eat meat, fish, eggs, or root vegetables
constraints.surface_form: Dev grew up in a Jain family in Gujarat and still follows all the traditions pretty closely
inference_chain: Jain family, follows traditions closely → practicing Jain
Jain dietary practice → strict vegetarian, no meat, no fish, no eggs, no root vegetables

hidden_state.value: You are planning a birthday dinner for your friend Sophie at a French bistro. You will introduce the guest list and their backgrounds across several turns. Plans will change: Marcus's celiac diagnosis gets reversed, Tom has to leave early, and Priya's husband Dev joins late. At the end, you will share a specific menu and ask if there are any issues. You must NEVER hint at what the problems might be — just ask openly.

You are a calm, upbeat friend organizing a birthday dinner. You always refer to your friends by name in third person (e.g. 'Marcus just messaged...', 'Tom texted me...'). You never express frustration or impatience when plans change — you treat it as normal friend-group coordination. Keep a warm but matter-of-fact tone.
hidden_state.description: Prevents emotion escalation and ensures third-person relay for friend updates

ground_truth.answer: Steak tartare is problematic: it is raw beef, which Sophie (pregnant) must avoid, and Dev (Jain) cannot eat meat. French onion soup with bread crust is problematic for Dev (contains beef broth typically, and onions are root vegetables forbidden for strict Jain practice). Lobster bisque is fine for the table — Tom (shellfish allergy) is no longer attending dinner, so no shellfish issue for diners; however it cannot be in Tom's dessert takeaway box (but it's not a dessert anyway). Mushroom and gruyère crêpes are fine for most but Dev (Jain) must be checked — mushrooms are fine for Jains, gruyère is vegetarian cheese, crêpes contain eggs which strict Jains avoid. Chocolate mousse typically contains raw eggs, which is problematic for Sophie (pregnancy — raw eggs) and for Dev (Jain — no eggs). Marcus has NO dietary restrictions anymore (celiac was a misdiagnosis). Tom's shellfish allergy no longer applies to the table since he is not attending dinner.

Steak tartare is problematic for Dev because it is meat and he follows Jain dietary practice

Mushroom and gruyère crêpes are problematic for Dev because crêpes contain eggs, which strict Jain practice forbids
Chocolate mousse is problematic for Sophie because it traditionally contains raw or lightly cooked eggs, which pregnant women should avoid
Chocolate mousse is problematic for Dev because it contains eggs, which Jain practice forbids

Flagging lobster bisque as problematic for the dinner table (Tom has left and is not dining)
Saying Tom has a general seafood allergy (he specifically has a shellfish allergy from shrimp anaphylaxis)
Ignoring Dev's Jain dietary constraints on any dish containing meat, eggs, or root vegetables
Ignoring Sophie's pregnancy restriction on raw meat or raw eggs
ground_truth.explanation: This scenario tests entity lifecycle tracking and inferential constraint reasoning across 9 conversational turns at a French bistro birthday dinner. The agent must track: (1) Marcus has celiac → no gluten (inferential), but this constraint is REMOVED mid-conversation (misdiagnosis reversed), (2) Tom has shellfish allergy from shrimp anaphylaxis (inferential: shrimp → shellfish), but Tom EXITS the dinner and only needs a dessert takeaway, so his shellfish allergy no longer applies to the table, (3) Sophie is 14 weeks pregnant → no raw meat, no raw eggs, no unpasteurized cheese (inferential), (4) Dev JOINS late as Priya's husband with an inferential constraint: Jain family from Gujarat, follows traditions closely → strict Jain vegetarian → no meat, no fish, no eggs, no root vegetables. At probe time, the current constraint state is: Sophie = pregnant (no raw meat, no raw eggs), Dev = Jain (no meat, no fish, no eggs, no root vegetables), Marcus = no restrictions, Tom = not at table. The 5 dishes have mixed verdicts: steak tartare (bad — raw meat hits Sophie + Dev), French onion soup (bad — beef broth + onions hit Dev), lobster bisque (fine for table — Tom is gone; trap item), mushroom gruyère crêpes (bad for Dev — eggs in crêpe batter), chocolate mousse (bad — raw eggs hit Sophie + Dev). The constraint REMOVAL (Marcus celiac reversed) is the primary difficulty mechanism, testing whether the agent stops flagging gluten for Marcus.

mechanism: Constraint REMOVAL: someone heals or a restriction is lifted mid-conversation
